comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
DIRECTION FROM OPERATOR: do not pin a local update tool. Recording the consequences, and a correction to my own earlier recommendation.

MY RECOMMENDATION WAS WRONG ON THE FACTS. I proposed 'brew upgrade uv' as the minimal unblock. That cannot work: required-version is '==0.12.7', an EXACT pin, and Homebrew has moved PAST it to 0.12.9 (2026-09-01). Verified empirically against a scratch pyproject carrying the same pin:
  /opt/homebrew/bin/uv 0.12.9  -> error: Required uv version `==0.12.7` does not match the running version `0.12.9`
  ~/.local/bin/uv     0.12.7  -> Resolved 1 package
Upgrading Homebrew only changes which number appears in the error. The scheduled 00:32 run confirms it independently: it failed with 0.12.9 and pushed the streak to 120. I should have checked the pin's comparison operator before recommending an upgrade.

THIS IS THE FEBD FAILURE, VERSION FOR VERSION. scripts/check_uv_pin.py's docstring describes the outage as: 'every build died with Required uv version ==0.12.7 does not match the running version 0.12.9 the moment :latest moved -- a time bomb armed by an upstream release, with no change to this repository.' The version in that sentence is 0.12.9, which is what Homebrew now ships. So this host's updater is the SAME time bomb with a different fuse: not a floating Docker tag, but a package manager that upgraded past the pin. Four consumers of one exact pin, three of which were never brought along.

RELAXING THE PIN IS NOT AVAILABLE. check_uv_pin.py deliberately fails the build when the pin is 'loosened to a range' (its point 2) or overridden per call site (point 3), because an exact pin is the property under test. So the fix cannot be a wider constraint in pyproject.toml.

WHAT THE DIRECTION MEANS FOR AC2. The updater is a local dev-tracking tool, not CI; it gains no reproducibility from being locked to any particular uv binary, and the current hardcode (UV_BIN default /opt/homebrew/bin/uv at rebar-dev-update.sh:18) is itself a local pin -- the one that broke. So AC2 stands as written and should be read as explicitly EXCLUDING a new hardcoded path: the updater must DERIVE the uv it needs from the CANDIDATE COMMIT's own required-version at sync time, since that value changes as main moves, and fail loudly naming required version, found version, and paths inspected when none satisfies it. Substituting one absolute path for another (either direction) is rejected -- it re-inverts the moment the other side updates first, which is exactly how this stall was born.

AC3 RESCOPED per operator decision: do NOT pursue the cross-account SNS authorization. The alert sink stays as-is. AC4 (a LOCAL detector that surfaces a stalled updater or an over-stale build without depending on the remote sink) absorbs the detection requirement and is the priority half -- it is the thing that would actually have caught 120 silent failures.

IMMEDIATE STATE: no persistent host change made. No plist edit, no REBAR_DEV_UV_BIN pin. Homebrew's uv did move 0.12.6 -> 0.12.9 during investigation (a relink surfaced by 'brew upgrade'; both versions fail the pin identically, so no behavior changed). The global rebar remains at cdfd7d94d and stale until AC2 lands or an operator runs a one-shot.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
AC4 (local detector) IMPLEMENTED and independently verified on this host. AC2 patch written but NOT applied -- awaiting operator decision, since the target is a machine-local script.

THE DETECTOR REPORTS THE REAL BUG. Verified by me directly, not taken on report:
  doctor: build freshness
    [error] reject-streak: the main-tracking updater has rejected 122 consecutive candidates (threshold 3) ...
    [error] build-stale: the published rebar build (cdfd7d94d, 2026-08-29) is 201 commit(s) behind origin/main (6125c5345), over the 25-commit threshold -- gate results from it can be wrong in ways the verdict cannot show
Note the numbers MOVED between the implementer's run and mine: streak 121 -> 122, drift 200 -> 201. The stall is ongoing and worsening hourly, which is itself corroboration.

SHAPE: a scan module inside the existing 'rebar doctor' command, NOT a new scripts/check_*.py. The check_orphaned_load.py precedent was weighed and SPLIT rather than copied: its ON-DEMAND half is exactly right (live host state is not a property of the tree under review, so it does not belong in make lint), but its LOCATION is not -- scripts/ is where this repo puts things that gate or report on the TREE. doctor_mcp_client.py is the closer structural match: it reads the operator's home directory, degrades every fault to a finding, renders its own section, and stays advisory outside the exit code and outside --repair. That contract was copied exactly, plus a has_blocking_build_freshness() seam for a caller that does want to gate. AC4 also names a 'rebar' invocation as its first example. Secondary argument, and a good one: an operator already runs 'rebar doctor', whereas a script nobody knows exists is a detector with the same silence problem as the dead SNS topic.

TWO INDEPENDENT SIGNALS, deliberately not one: reject-streak catches an updater that is FAILING; build-stale (>25 commits behind) catches one that STOPPED RUNNING, and survives a hand-reset counter. Threshold justified from data rather than picked: a healthy hourly updater sits 0-2 commits behind, and the two recorded incidents were ~48 and ~195, so 25 is below the smaller incident and an order of magnitude above healthy.

REUSE, NOT REIMPLEMENTATION: the commit-distance walk is build_drift.detect_drift, extended with one keyword-only build_sha parameter defaulting to running_build_sha(). It previously read only the RUNNING process's sha, which cannot answer 'how stale is the build the updater published' from a dev checkout. All existing callers unchanged.

NO NEW MECHANISM. _detect_gate_scripts was checked BEFORE designing (it names a ci_gate by the repo-relative path of any scripts/check_*.py), which is precisely why the detector is not one. check_mechanism_delta.py --check reports new=0, and test_mechanism_delta.py passes 31/31. No marker, no baseline edit.

A GATE CAUGHT A DESIGN FICTION, worth recording as a positive: the first draft read XDG_STATE_HOME, which check_config_ownership.py rejected as an 'unresolved-env-read below approved seam'. Rather than add a marker to keep it, the env read was REMOVED -- because the updater itself does not consult XDG_STATE_HOME (its default is ${HOME}/.local/state/rebar-dev), so honoring it described a layout that is never written. The module now reads no environment at all. The gate did not just block a violation; it surfaced that the code was accommodating something fictional. Documented limitation: an operator who relocated state via the updater's own REBAR_DEV_STATE_DIR passes state_dir= to the scan.

Verification: make lint exit 0; make typecheck clean (755 files); test_mechanism_delta.py 31 passed; 110 targeted passed; 102 regression passed. RED first: ImportError for the absent module, then 14 passed.

AC2 PATCH READY BUT UNAPPLIED. Live ~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh confirmed byte-identical to its original. It honors the operator's direction -- no pinned local tool, and no substituted absolute path: UV_BIN's hardcoded default is removed, REBAR_DEV_UV_BIN survives only as a HINT that is validated like any other candidate rather than trusted, and the pin is read from the CANDIDATE COMMIT's own pyproject.toml AFTER checkout (the earliest point it exists, and why the value tracks main rather than this host). Every uv on PATH is probed by --version and the first exact match wins, so PATH ORDER STOPS BEING LOAD-BEARING in either direction. Exact string comparison suffices without a version solver because check_uv_pin.py contractually guarantees an exact ==X.Y.Z and fails the build on a range; any other shape is refused loudly rather than guessed.

Exercised against the real host (functions extracted to a harness; the updater itself never run):
  real pyproject ==0.12.7  -> selects ~/.local/bin/uv, THE BINARY THE CURRENT HARDCODE EXCLUDES
  unsatisfiable ==9.9.9    -> names required version, every version found, and every path inspected
  wrong hint (0.12.9)      -> rejected, correct 0.12.7 chosen (validated, not trusted)
  range pin / no pin       -> refused loudly
Failures now reject at a new 'uv-select' stage, so the log and reject-streak name binary selection rather than blaming sync.

AC1 depends on AC2 being applied (operator's call). AC3 was rescoped away by the operator. AC5 (pruner 'Directory not empty' and the 5fb69334...1559 partial-release stub) remains open and untouched.

AC2 HAS NO REPO-SIDE TEST and cannot have one: the script is machine-local and git-ignored, so nothing in the tree can reach it. The evidence is the harness run above.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
INCIDENT DETAIL MOVED OUT OF THE DESCRIPTION (nothing deleted — preserved here verbatim in substance).

Reason for the move: `review-plan` BLOCKED the ticket on two deterministic criteria (P1 readiness-shape: no `## Acceptance Criteria` heading with `- [ ]` items; P10 verification-presence: no `## Testing` section and no AC naming a proving command), and the description was at 7,556 of the 8,000-character admission cap (P4) — only 444 characters of headroom. Adding the required structure was impossible without first moving narrative into a comment. The description now carries the plan and its acceptance criteria; the forensic detail lives here.

## Root cause, in full

`~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh:18` hardcodes the uv binary:

    UV_BIN="${REBAR_DEV_UV_BIN:-/opt/homebrew/bin/uv}"

and `:120` orders PATH to keep it authoritative, reasoning at `:116-118`:

    # launchd gives a minimal PATH. Keep Homebrew before ~/.local/bin so the obsolete
    # standalone uv there cannot shadow the pinned UV_BIN.
    export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:${HOME}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"

Measured on this host: `/opt/homebrew/bin/uv` is 0.12.9 (Homebrew moved 0.12.6 -> 0.12.9 during investigation); `/Users/joeoakhart/.local/bin/uv` is 0.12.7 (standalone, 2026-08-27). `pyproject.toml` pins `required-version = "==0.12.7"` (commit 7501cc1d602d). uv reads `required-version` itself and fails fast, so `:344`'s `"$UV_BIN" sync` aborts every run.

THE COMMENT'S PREMISE INVERTED. When written, `~/.local/bin` held the obsolete uv, so pinning to Homebrew was right. Homebrew is now the stale side. The guard written to stop a stale uv being selected became the mechanism selecting one. Hardcoding EITHER absolute path re-inverts the next time one side updates first — which is why AC2 requires derivation, not substitution.

## This is the febd failure, version for version

`scripts/check_uv_pin.py`'s docstring describes that outage: "every build died with `Required uv version ==0.12.7 does not match the running version 0.12.9` the moment `:latest` moved — a time bomb armed by an upstream release, with no change to this repository." The version in that sentence, 0.12.9, is what Homebrew now ships. Same exact pin, same version, different fuse: a package manager that upgraded past the pin rather than a floating Docker tag. Four consumers of one pin; three were never brought along.

RELAXING THE PIN IS NOT AVAILABLE: `check_uv_pin.py` fails the build when the pin is loosened to a range (its point 2) or overridden per call site (point 3). An exact pin is the property under test.

## The alert that should have caught this

`REJECT_STREAK_ALERT` (default 3) was added after "the b477339a99 incident: 43 hourly `sync` rejections, ~48 commits behind, no signal". It fired correctly and failed to deliver every time:

    aws: [ERROR]: An error occurred (AuthorizationError) when calling the Publish operation:
    User: arn:aws:iam::820258254566:user/joeoakhart is not authorized to perform: SNS:Publish
    on resource: arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:896586841071:rebar-gerrit-alerts

IAM principal in account 820258254566; topic in 896586841071; no resource-based policy permits the cross-account publish. The streak reached 120+ against a threshold of 3 with zero operator signal.

## Impact

Every agent session on this host invoking the global `rebar` ran a build ~195 commits stale for about five days. The gate's own advisory: "this rebar build (cdfd7d94d, 2026-08-29, dirty) is 195 commit(s) BEHIND the ref this gate pinned (08a39c39c) — it may predate recent config keys and gate fixes, so results can be wrong in ways the verdict cannot show." That reaches plan-review and completion-verifier verdicts produced through the global tool. Noticed only because a subagent's gate log was read closely.

## Secondary defect (AC5)

`launchd.err.log` shows the pruner failing to reclaim release dirs:

    rm: .../releases/5b5008bbfbec...66068/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages: Directory not empty
    rm: .../releases/5fb693345b0c...1559: Directory not empty

`releases/5fb693345b0cd1b48d1e9d20b292fd15761c7624.1559` is a 3-entry stub — a partially built release never completed or cleaned. Related to the disk-ceiling work under epic 6202-e1c7-c57f-4897; these dirs are ~346 MB each.

## Ongoing

The stall is live and worsening: reject-streak 121 -> 122 and drift 200 -> 201 commits were observed within a single working session.

AC4 pushed for review: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2608 (commit f50dc1007bd0, Change-Id I55bc93a0a81b4dcd011c733b02e6d9dac3a9cf34).

SCOPE OF THIS CHANGE: AC4 ONLY. rebar doctor gains a build-freshness section reading two independent local signals -- reject-streak (the updater's own counter vs its threshold of 3) and build-stale (the build behind the current pointer more than 25 commits behind origin/main). No network, no credential, no CI provider. Advisory: printed in text and JSON, outside doctor's exit code and outside --repair, on the same grounds doctor already applies to HOME-sourced MCP-client findings. Absent updater state emits one 'unavailable' finding, never a failure.

Files: src/rebar/_commands/doctor_build_freshness.py (new), src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py (wiring), src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py (optional build_sha so the EXISTING ancestry walk can measure a build this process is not executing -- reuse, not a second walk), tests/unit/test_doctor_build_freshness.py (new, RED-first), docs/user-guide.md.

NO NEW MECHANISM. A scripts/check_*.py would have registered a ci_gate named by its path (scripts/_mechanism_delta/detect_ci.py::_detect_gate_scripts), which --check admits via a marker but tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py rejects regardless (the contradiction filed as a1f1-a30d-2d50-4f5a). Delivering this inside the existing rebar doctor command avoids the kind entirely: check_mechanism_delta.py --check reports new=0 increased=0 stale=0 and test_mechanism_delta.py passes 31/31. No marker added, no baseline edited.

An XDG_STATE_HOME read was REMOVED rather than marked: check_config_ownership.py flagged it as an unresolved-env-read below an approved seam, and the updater does not consult that variable anyway, so the code was accommodating a layout that is never written. The module now reads no environment at all.

GATES: review-plan PASS and SIGNED at head_sha f50dc1007bd0 (verified_at_sha 6125c5345f01). Three runs: run 1 blocked deterministically in 6s with no LLM spend (P1 readiness-shape, P10 verification-presence); run 2 blocked on one LLM finding (AC4 named no staleness threshold); run 3 passed. The description was rewritten to the standard checklist shape and the incident forensics moved to the preceding comment -- it was at 7,556 of the 8,000-char admission cap with 444 chars of headroom, so the required structure could not be added without moving narrative out. file_impact recorded across the 5 files.

Verification: make lint exit 0 (ruff, complexity new=0 increased=0, mechanism new=0, config-ownership, uv-pin, zizmor, actionlint); make typecheck clean over 755 files; 110 targeted tests + 102 regression tests pass. On this host the detector reports the live bug: reject-streak 122, build-stale 201 commits, both climbing hourly.

STILL OPEN: AC1 and AC2 (with the operator as an unapplied diff to the machine-local, git-ignored rebar-dev-update.sh -- outside any repository test's reach) and AC5 (pruner Directory-not-empty + the 5fb69334...1559 stub). AC3 withdrawn by operator decision. NOT closing this ticket.

Carried advisory from run 3, recorded rather than actioned: build_drift.detect_drift performs no fetch, so origin/main is whatever the local checkout last fetched -- a checkout that has not fetched recently UNDERSTATES drift. That is the conservative direction (it never invents drift) and is documented at the TRACKED_REF constant, but a future change could resolve the ref via a bounded best-effort git ls-remote degrading to unavailable.

AC1 SATISFIED -- THE STALL IS OVER. AC2 patch applied to ~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh with operator approval, original backed up to rebar-dev-update.sh.pre-ac97.bak, and the updater run once to verify on the real thing rather than a harness.

Result:
  2026-09-04T05:06:47Z updated -> 6125c5345f0117d377acf72975c7c547316e537a (locked runtime; click override from uv.lock)
  2026-09-04T05:06:46Z prune summary: pruned=2 kept-live=0 remaining=4 (keep=3 cap=10)
  reject-streak: 122 -> 0
  current: releases/cdfd7d94d... (2026-08-28) -> releases/6125c5345f01... (current main)

So 122 consecutive failures and 201 commits of drift are ended, and the run also reclaimed two stale
release directories on its way through. Every session on this host now gets gate verdicts from
current code rather than a five-day-old build; the on-box MCP server is likewise no longer serving
stale gate code.

APPLICATION NOTE for whoever repeats this: 'git apply' REFUSES the diff because it names orig.sh /
new.sh -- it was generated from an extraction harness, not from a checkout. Use patch(1) against the
target explicitly: patch ~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh < <diff>. It applied cleanly, bash -n is
clean, and the hardcode at :18 is now UV_BIN="" with selection at :190.

WHY THIS FIX SHOULD NOT RE-INVERT, restated now that it is live: no absolute path is baked in.
PATH ORDER IS NO LONGER LOAD-BEARING -- every uv on PATH is probed by --version and the first exact
match wins, so neither Homebrew nor ~/.local/bin can shadow a satisfying binary in either direction.
The pin is read from the CANDIDATE COMMIT's own pyproject.toml after checkout, so it tracks main
rather than this host, which is the property the old hardcode lacked. REBAR_DEV_UV_BIN survives only
as a hint that is validated like any other candidate, never trusted.

STILL OPEN ON THIS TICKET:
 - AC4's detector is pushed for review as Gerrit change 2608 (not yet voted). Note it will now report
   CLEAN on this host, which is correct -- its live-host reading was already demoted to a one-time
   recorded datum (122 / 201 on 2026-09-03) precisely because AC1 destroys the observable condition.
   That AC-ordering fix has now paid off in practice rather than in theory.
 - AC5 (pruner 'Directory not empty' failures, and the 5fb693345b0c...1559 partial-release stub)
   remains open and untouched. Today's run pruned two releases successfully, so it is worth
   re-checking whether AC5 still reproduces before scoping work for it.
 - AC3 stays withdrawn per operator decision; AC4 absorbs its detection requirement.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
AC4 RESCOPED -- change 2608 ABANDONED after operator rejection, and the rejection is correct.

The objection: 'This contaminates rebar documentation with local environment setup relevant only to a specific user.'

That is right, and I should have caught it when I wrote the brief. The detector reads
~/.local/state/rebar-dev/ plus the reject-streak and current files written by this host's
main-tracking LaunchAgent. That updater is MACHINE-LOCAL -- it is documented in
docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md, which is git-ignored precisely because it is one operator's
setup rather than rebar behaviour. Shipping a 'rebar doctor' scan for it, plus a docs/user-guide.md
section, puts that setup into the product and into documentation every user reads.

WHAT I CONFLATED, and this is the useful distinction going forward:
 - A GENERAL capability: warn when the installed rebar is far behind main. That could affect any
   developer with a stale pipx/uv install and is arguably worth having.
 - A SPECIFIC one: read THIS HOST'S updater state files to detect THIS HOST'S LaunchAgent stalling.
The change implemented the general shape on top of the specific paths, which is why it looked
reasonable and was still wrong. Note the implementing agent had already removed an XDG_STATE_HOME
read after the config-ownership gate objected -- the right instinct, applied one level too shallow.

AC4 IS REPLACED BY:
 4. A stalled main-tracking updater is detectable WITHOUT depending on the remote alert sink, by a
    mechanism that lives OUTSIDE this repository's shipped surface -- e.g. in the machine-local
    tooling alongside rebar-dev-update.sh, or in the LaunchAgent itself. It must add nothing to
    rebar's CLI, its docs, or its public API. Verified by running it on this host and observing it
    report the real state.
 4b. If a GENERAL 'your installed build is N commits behind' capability is wanted in rebar proper,
    that is a SEPARATE ticket and a separate change. It must reference no machine-local paths and no
    LaunchAgent state, and must degrade to 'not applicable' wherever such state is absent. Do not
    fold it back in here.

STATE OF THIS BUG: AC1 and AC2 are effectively resolved -- the updater had failed 122 consecutive
runs and, after the patch was applied, published 6125c5345f01 with reject-streak back to 0. AC3 was
withdrawn by operator decision. AC5 (pruner 'Directory not empty' and the partial-release stub)
remains open and untouched. So what is left here is AC4's replacement and AC5.

Not closing: the remaining work is real, and closing on the strength of the half that landed would
overstate it.

## WARNING TO ANY FUTURE DISPATCH: this ticket's recorded file_impact is the ABANDONED design

Do not brief an implementation agent off this ticket's `file_impact`. It still lists
`src/rebar/_commands/doctor_build_freshness.py`, `doctor.py`, `src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py`,
`tests/unit/test_doctor_build_freshness.py` and `docs/user-guide.md` — the design in change 2608,
which the OPERATOR REJECTED and which was abandoned. Building against it would recreate the
rejected change.

The rejection reason matters and is binding: a `rebar doctor` check that reads THIS host's
LaunchAgent state contaminates rebar's shipped documentation and surface with one operator's local
environment setup. AC4's replacement therefore requires the detector to live **outside this
repository's shipped surface**. No in-repo path can satisfy it, which is precisely why the recorded
impact is not merely stale but actively wrong.

I am leaving `file_impact` unchanged rather than guessing a replacement: the out-of-repo design has
not been decided, and fabricating a plausible-looking path would be worse than an obviously stale
one. This comment is the guard.

## Actual AC state, which the checkboxes do not reflect

All five ACs still read `[ ]`, but per the comment history:

- **AC1 is SATISFIED.** The stall is over — the updater was patched with operator approval, ran to
  `6125c5345f01`, and the reject-streak went 122 -> 0, ending 201 commits of drift.
- **AC3 is WITHDRAWN** by operator decision (cross-account SNS).
- **AC4 is RESCOPED** as above, and needs an out-of-repo home before any implementation.

So this ticket is much closer to done than its checkbox state suggests, and what remains is a
design decision rather than an implementation task. That combination — advanced work behind
unchecked boxes plus misleading file_impact — is exactly the shape that has caused wasted
dispatches on this board twice already (this ticket and bff5).

## Recommendation

Do not dispatch a fix agent. This needs an operator call on where the freshness detector should
live, after which AC4 can be re-specified and the file_impact corrected in the same edit.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## OPERATOR DECISION on AC4: the LaunchAgent SELF-REPORTS

The updater emits its own freshness signal — a log line, a metric, or a file — that anything can
read, rather than rebar reaching in to inspect LaunchAgent state.

**This inverts the dependency, which is the point.** No rebar code needs to know that LaunchAgents
exist, so nothing about one operator's local setup enters rebar's shipped surface. That was the
operator's stated objection when change 2608 was rejected: a `rebar doctor` check reading this
host's LaunchAgent state contaminates shipped documentation and the product surface with
environment specific to a single machine.

It also satisfies AC4's replacement requirement — the detector lives OUTSIDE this repository's
shipped surface — without needing a separate repo or an undiscoverable machine-local script.

## Consequences for this ticket

**The recorded file_impact is now definitively wrong and must be replaced before any dispatch.** It
still lists `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_build_freshness.py`, `doctor.py`,
`src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py`, `tests/unit/test_doctor_build_freshness.py` and
`docs/user-guide.md` — the abandoned change-2608 design. Under this decision **no in-repo path is
correct**, because the emitter is the LaunchAgent, not rebar.

Whoever picks this up should record the impact against wherever the updater's own definition lives
(the LaunchAgent plist / its script), which is outside this repo, and may legitimately be a
`--none` file-impact declaration with a reason if nothing shipped changes at all.

**AC state recap** (the checkboxes still read unchecked and do not reflect reality):
- AC1 SATISFIED — the stall is over; the updater was patched with operator approval, ran to
  6125c5345f01, and the reject-streak went 122 -> 0, ending 201 commits of drift.
- AC3 WITHDRAWN by operator decision (cross-account SNS).
- AC4 now has its design decided (this comment) but is NOT yet implemented.

## Open design question left to the implementer, not decided here

What the emitted signal should BE. A CloudWatch metric would page through the existing alarm path
but adds an AWS dependency to a local tool; a log line is cheapest but needs something to read it;
a file is simplest and pairs naturally with a `rebar doctor` check that reads a GENERIC path
rather than a LaunchAgent-specific one. The operator chose the direction (self-report), not the
transport.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Evidence that the updater is LIVE, and a newly-observed cost — both from tonight, both partly in
tension with this ticket's "stalled 119 runs" framing.

## The updater is running and reinstalling

```
ls -la $(which rebar)
-rwxr-xr-x  1 joeoakhart  staff  1179  Sep  4 20:42  /Users/joeoakhart/.local/bin/rebar
```

That mtime is ~40 minutes before this comment, so the LaunchAgent is not merely loaded, it is
reinstalling. `launchctl list` shows all three agents present with last exit status **0** and no
live PID:

```
-  0  com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update
-  0  com.navapbc.rebar-worktree-gc
-  0  com.navapbc.rebar-serena-mirror-update
```

So "stalled on a uv version mismatch" is either resolved, or was intermittent, or the stall
coexists with a successful reinstall path. Worth establishing which before this ticket's fix is
designed — a fix aimed at a permanently-wedged updater would be aimed at the wrong thing.

## The newly-observed cost: it appears to kill in-flight gate runs

An agent working the Windows epic tonight reported, unprompted:

> Gate daemons died four times (`stale-running`), plus one `transport dropped mid-call`.
> Consistent with this host's hourly LaunchAgent reinstalling `rebar-mcp` mid-review. A dead run
> is indistinguishable from a live one without polling `gate_status`.

Combined with the mtime above, the mechanism is plausible: the updater replaces the `rebar-mcp`
that a background gate daemon is running inside, and the run dies holding nothing. Each death
costs a **billable LLM gate pass** and leaves a `stale-running` handle that looks identical to a
live run — the failure is silent unless someone polls.

**This is a hypothesis, not a finding.** It has not been reproduced by deliberately triggering a
reinstall during a gate run, and gate runs did succeed repeatedly tonight (four ticket closes and
several plan reviews completed), so the interaction is at most intermittent. The decisive
experiment is cheap: start a `review_plan_start`, force a sync with
`launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`, and poll `gate_status` for
`stale-running`.

## Not acted on

I deliberately did NOT pause the LaunchAgent. Gates are succeeding often enough that a
preemptive change to this machine's configuration is not needed to complete the work, and the
mechanism is unproven. Recording it so the operator can decide with the evidence in hand, and so
the next session that loses a gate run has somewhere to look first.

Also noting for whoever picks this up: `com.navapbc.rebar-worktree-gc` exists alongside the
updater. Several agent worktrees are live on this host tonight with unpushed work in them; if that
GC reaps a worktree an agent is mid-change in, the symptom would look nothing like an updater
problem.

comments.body:
## Measured state 2026-09-05 ~18:50 — the "stalled 120 runs" premise no longer holds

Measured directly rather than inferred, because this ticket was about to be dispatched on its stated premise:

```
global rebar:  /Users/joeoakhart/.local/bin/rebar   mtime Sep  5 11:40   (~7h ago)
launchctl:     com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update    last exit status 0
               com.navapbc.rebar-worktree-gc   running (pid 75958)
               com.navapbc.rebar-serena-mirror-update   exit 0
uv:            /opt/homebrew/bin/uv        0.12.9  (Homebrew 2026-09-01)
               ~/.local/bin/uv             0.12.7
pipx:          nava-rebar 0.10.1
```

The updater is **reinstalling and exiting 0**, so the `required-version ==0.12.7` rejection loop described in the Root cause section is NOT currently firing. This corroborates the earlier comment that flagged the "stalled 119 runs" framing as in tension with observed evidence. The `UV_BIN` hardcoding may still be a latent defect — both uv builds are present and the ordering could invert again on the next Homebrew bump — but it is not producing a live stall right now. **Whoever claims this should re-derive the current failure mode before fixing the one in the description.**

## Direct evidence FOR AC4, obtained by failing to satisfy it manually

AC4 asks that "a stalled updater or an over-stale build is detectable locally". I attempted exactly that detection by hand and could not:

- `rebar --version` -> `Error: unknown subcommand '--version'`
- `~/.local/pipx/venvs/nava-rebar` exists, but has **no `direct_url.json`**, so the installed VCS commit is not recoverable from package metadata
- the only staleness signal available is the binary's **mtime**, which reports when the install last ran, NOT which commit it installed

So an operator (or an agent) currently has no way to answer "how far behind `origin/main` is the global build?" without reading updater logs that may have rotated. That is the gap AC4 names, demonstrated rather than asserted. The AC4 design already agreed with the operator — the LaunchAgent SELF-REPORTS a freshness signal rather than rebar inspecting LaunchAgent state — and this measurement supports that shape: what is missing is a durable, readable record of the installed commit, not a launchd probe.

## Disposition this tick

NOT dispatched. Reasons: the p1 urgency in the description is disproven by the measurement above; the remaining value is the AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 detector work, whose file impact (`src/rebar/_commands/doctor*.py`, `src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py`) risks overlap with two agents currently working in `src/rebar/**`; and host capacity is committed to the duplicate-producer RCA (`anarchic-princely-raven`), which gates re-enabling the reconcile bridge.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## CORRECTION to my previous comment — the capability EXISTS, it is just not surfaced

Earlier in this session I wrote that an operator "currently has no way to answer how far behind
`origin/main` the global build is", citing the absence of `rebar --version` and of a
`direct_url.json` in the pipx venv. **That was overstated, and the evidence against it came from
rebar itself.**

Closing `ae96-72a9-8145-4c85` emitted, unprompted:

```
WARNING rebar.llm.build_drift: this rebar build (e510c64db, 2026-09-05, dirty) is 37 commit(s)
BEHIND the ref this gate pinned (4c9940348) — it may predate recent config keys and gate fixes,
so results can be wrong in ways the verdict cannot show.
```

So rebar CAN identify its own build commit and compute a commit delta. Reading the module:

- `src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:117` `running_build_sha()` — "the commit of the rebar build
  executing this process", delegating to `rebar.signing._gate_commit_sha`. This is precisely the
  fact I claimed was unrecoverable.
- `BuildDrift` carries `build_sha`, `pinned_sha`, `build_date`, and `commits_behind` (full
  40-char SHAs, resolved in the target repo so they are directly comparable).
- Sole caller: `src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:147` `build_drift.warn_if_behind(handle.sha,
  repo_root)`. It runs ONLY inside a gate that pins a ref, and `detect_drift` returns `None` for
  a `local`-source gate, which pins nothing.

## What this changes for AC4

AC4 is smaller than I described. It is NOT "invent a way to know the installed commit" — that
exists. It is:

1. **Surface it outside gate ops.** The signal is emitted as a `WARNING` log line during a gate
   and nowhere else, so an operator who is not running a gate never sees it.
2. **Compare against the right reference.** Today the comparison is build-vs-*the gate's pinned
   ref*. The staleness question this ticket cares about is build-vs-`origin/main`.
3. **Note the scope difference.** The warning above reports the REPO VENV build (`e510c64db`,
   `dirty`), not the GLOBAL pipx build (`nava-rebar`). Whether `running_build_sha()` resolves
   usefully for a non-editable pipx install is UNVERIFIED by me and should be checked first — it
   may return `None` there, which would be the actual gap.

This ticket's `file_impact` already names `src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py`, so the intended fix was
presumably always to extend this mechanism. My previous comment made the gap sound larger than it
is; whoever claims this should start from `running_build_sha()` rather than building anything new.

comments.author: rebar review bot
comments.body:
## AC4 withdrawn from the shipped surface — change 3014 abandoned

Operator decision: abandon, do not rework.

Gerrit change 3014 is abandoned, for the same reason change 2608 was. Both
implemented AC4 as it was written, and AC4 as written required reading
`~/.local/state/rebar-dev/` — the reject-streak counter and `current` pointer
produced by this host's main-tracking LaunchAgent. That setup is documented in
`docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md`, git-ignored because it is one
operator's machine configuration rather than rebar behaviour. A `rebar doctor`
scan for it, plus a `docs/user-guide.md` section, would ship that configuration
as product.

The two rejections came from opposite directions, which is worth recording
because it shows the fault was in the AC rather than in either implementation:

- **2608** — operator `Code-Review-1`, abandoned. The detector read the
  machine-local state files directly.
- **3014 patch set 1** — `LLM-Review-1`. `scan_build_freshness(repo_root=...)`
  measured the updater's published SHA against the *doctor caller's* store repo,
  comparing two unrelated repositories.
- **3014 patch set 2** — `LLM-Review-1` again, scope-intent. The fix for patch
  set 1 added an updater-state `source-repo` lookup, which moved further into
  the machine-local dependency rather than out of it.

The rescope promised in 2608's abandon message ("I am rescoping AC4") was never
written into this ticket's description. That is why the second attempt
reproduced the first one's rejection: the text being implemented still demanded
the rejected design. AC4 has now been rewritten to record the withdrawal, and is
tagged `[non-codebase]` because its done-evidence is a decision on those two
Gerrit changes, not an artifact in this tree.

## The general capability is a separate ticket, deliberately not tracked here

The 2608 decision distinguished two things that had been conflated: a SPECIFIC
detector for this host's updater, which does not belong in the shipped surface
at all, and a GENERAL check — warn when the installed rebar is far behind `main`
— which could affect any developer with a stale install.

The general one remains plausible and needs its own ticket. It would not start
from scratch: `rebar.llm.build_drift.running_build_sha()` already resolves the
running build's commit, and `BuildDrift` already carries `commits_behind`
against a pinned ref with full 40-character SHAs. This very session saw it fire
unprompted while closing `794e`:

```
WARNING rebar.llm.build_drift: this rebar build (e900fa14a, 2026-09-19, dirty)
is 25 commit(s) BEHIND the ref this gate pinned (204c60697)
```

Its only caller today is `gate_source.py`, so it runs only inside a gate that
pins a ref. Surfacing it elsewhere is the feature; nothing new needs inventing,
and no machine-local path is involved.

## What remains on this ticket

AC3 is already WITHDRAWN by operator decision, and AC4 is now withdrawn too.
That leaves AC1/AC2 (the updater's kickstart and uv selection, which the 2608
abandon message records as already resolved — the updater had failed 122
consecutive runs and is publishing current builds again) and **AC5**, the
pruner's `Directory not empty` failures and the partial-directory cleanup. AC5
is untouched by any of this and is the live remaining work.

comments.body:
## AC5 settled: its subject was REMOVED from this host, not repaired

Measured directly on 2026-09-20 with the sandbox lifted, so these are real `ENOENT`
results rather than denied reads. An earlier pass in this session reported the same paths
as missing while `~/.local/` was sandbox-blocked; that reading was not trustworthy and is
superseded by what follows. A control probe confirms the difference: `~/.local`,
`~/.local/state`, `~/.local/bin` and `~/.local/share` all resolve as EXISTING, while every
path below is genuinely absent.

```
~/.local/state/rebar-dev                     No such file or directory
~/.local/state/rebar-dev/releases            No such file or directory
~/.local/state/rebar-dev/current/sha         No such file or directory
~/.local/state/rebar-dev/reject-streak       No such file or directory
~/.local/state/rebar-dev/launchd.err.log     No such file or directory
~/.local/state/rebar-dev/update.log          No such file or directory
~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh             MISSING
~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh.pre-ac97.bak MISSING
```

The updater was not merely unloaded. The script, its `.pre-ac97.bak` backup created by
this ticket's own AC2 fix, its entire state tree, and its LaunchAgent are all gone:

```
~/Library/LaunchAgents/   com.joeoakhart.agent-config-backup.plist
                          com.joeoakhart.agent-skills-update.plist
                          com.joeoakhart.secrets-load.plist
                          (dir mtime Sep 12 00:54)
launchctl list | grep -iE 'navapbc|rebar'   -> no match
find ~ -name 'rebar-dev-update*' -o -name 'com.navapbc.rebar*'   -> no match
find ~ -type d -name 'rebar-dev'   -> no match
find ~ -name 'local-env-main-tracking*'   -> no match
```

All three `com.navapbc.rebar-*` agents that earlier comments recorded at exit 0 —
`rebar-dev-update`, `rebar-worktree-gc`, `rebar-serena-mirror-update` — are absent.
`docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md` is gone as well, with no git history, which is
expected for a git-ignored file.

## Why AC5 is marked `[non-codebase]` rather than ticked as fixed

AC5's two checks both pass, but VACUOUSLY. The `5fb693345b0cd...1559` stub is absent
because the whole `releases` tree is absent, and `Directory not empty` cannot appear in a
`launchd.err.log` that does not exist. That is not evidence the pruner was repaired, and
recording it as such would assert something untrue.

## Restore was attempted first and is not available

Per operator decision the preferred path was to restore the updater and verify AC5 against
a live pruner. `~/Desktop/backup` was inspected for that purpose and carries neither
`.local/` nor `Library/`, so it never captured the updater, its state, or its plist. No
other copy exists anywhere under `$HOME`. Rebuilding the script from scratch would be
authoring a NEW machine-local tool rather than restoring one, and this ticket is not the
place for that.

## What this ticket actually fixed, and why it closes as env_integration

The reported defect was real, root-caused, and fixed. AC1 and AC2 are satisfied by
evidence already recorded above: the uv pin is now read from the CANDIDATE COMMIT's own
`pyproject.toml` rather than hardcoded, no absolute path is baked in, PATH order is no
longer load-bearing, and the live updater run took `reject-streak` from 122 to 0 while
advancing `current` to `6125c5345f01`, ending 201 commits of drift. AC3 was withdrawn by
operator decision (cross-account SNS not pursued). AC4 was withdrawn from rebar's shipped
surface across two rejected changes, 2608 and 3014, and is recorded as `[non-codebase]`.

The root cause was an exact uv `required-version` pin interacting with the versions
available on one host — an environment/integration defect, not a defect in rebar's own
logic. Hence `env_integration`.

## Adjacent finding, deliberately NOT tracked here

This host has had no main-tracking updater since approximately 2026-09-12. The global
`rebar` symlink was last written Sep 14 19:45. Gates run from a repository worktree venv
and are unaffected, but anything invoking the global `rebar` gets that older build. If the
removal was not deliberate, restoring main-tracking is separate work needing its own
ticket; AGENTS.md places that tooling outside this repository.

compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

The hourly LaunchAgent `com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`, which keeps this host's **global**
`rebar` / `rebar-mcp` aligned to `origin/main`, has failed 120+ consecutive times and is
still failing. The global build is pinned at `cdfd7d94dc2fe7671a7eba48e31f36c30f39235c`
(2026-08-28) — 201 commits behind `origin/main` at the latest check, and climbing hourly.
`launchctl list` reports last exit status 1 for the agent.

Every hourly run logs the same rejection:

```
error: Required uv version `==0.12.7` does not match the running version `0.12.9`
candidate ebbcd7a030d6... rejected at sync; current left untouched
candidate-rejection streak now 122 (latest stage: sync)
```

## Root cause

`~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh:18` hardcodes `UV_BIN` to an absolute Homebrew path and
`:120` orders PATH to keep it authoritative. That premise has INVERTED: Homebrew's uv is now
0.12.9, past the repository's exact `required-version = "==0.12.7"`, while the
`~/.local/bin` standalone sits at 0.12.7. The guard written to stop a stale uv being
selected is now the mechanism selecting one. Substituting the other absolute path
re-inverts the moment that side updates first. Full forensics — the `febd` precedent, the
SNS failure, and the impact measurement — are preserved in the ticket comments.

## The detection gap is the priority half

`REJECT_STREAK_ALERT` (threshold 3) fired every hour and failed to deliver every time: the
IAM principal is in account 820258254566, the SNS topic in 896586841071, and no
resource-based policy permits the cross-account publish. The streak therefore reached 120+
against a threshold of 3 with zero operator signal. Whatever causes the next stall, it is
equally silent unless a detector exists that does not depend on a remote sink.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 — An on-demand `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`
  publishes a `current` whose sha equals `origin/main` at that moment. Checked by
  `[ "$(cat ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/current/sha)" = "$(git ls-remote origin main | cut -f1)" ]`,
  by `! grep -q '^error: Required uv version' ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/update.log`, and by
  `[ "$(cat ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/reject-streak)" -eq 0 ]`.
- [x] AC2 — The updater selects a uv satisfying the CANDIDATE COMMIT's own
  `required-version`, read from that commit's `pyproject.toml` at sync time, rather than any
  hardcoded absolute path. When no available uv satisfies it, the run fails with a message
  naming the required version, each version found, and each path inspected. DISPOSITION of
  that failure is a SOFT RETRY, not a terminal stop: the candidate is rejected at its own
  `uv-select` stage, `current` is left untouched, the streak increments, and the next hourly
  tick retries — matching the existing `rejected at sync; current left untouched` behaviour,
  so a since-fixed or transient pin heals without operator action. Checked by running the
  resolver against a checkout whose pin no local uv satisfies and asserting the message
  names all three facts, and against one whose pin is satisfiable and asserting it selects
  that uv.
- [x] AC3 — WITHDRAWN by operator decision: the cross-account SNS authorization is not
  being pursued and the sink stays as-is. AC4 absorbs the detection requirement.
- [x] AC4 [non-codebase] — WITHDRAWN from rebar's shipped surface by operator
  decision on Gerrit change 2608, reaffirmed on change 3014. Detection of a stalled updater
  or an over-stale build lives in the LOCAL-ONLY tooling OUTSIDE this repository, not in
  `rebar doctor` and not in `docs/user-guide.md`.

  The original wording required two signals sourced from the host's main-tracking
  LaunchAgent: `reject-streak` (that updater's own counter) and `build-stale` (measured
  against that updater's `current` pointer). Both read `~/.local/state/rebar-dev/`, written
  by a setup described in `docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md` — a file that is
  git-ignored precisely because it is one operator's machine configuration rather than rebar
  behaviour. Shipping a scan for it would put that configuration into the product and into
  documentation every user reads.

  Two changes implemented this AC as written and both were rejected for it: 2608 (operator
  `Code-Review-1`, abandoned) and 3014 (`LLM-Review-1`, scope-intent, abandoned). The
  rescope promised on 2608 was never written into this description, which is why the second
  attempt reproduced the first one's rejection.

  A GENERAL capability — warn when the installed rebar is far behind `main`, affecting any
  developer with a stale install — remains plausible and is explicitly a SEPARATE FEATURE
  requiring its own ticket. It must reference no machine-local paths. It would not start
  from scratch: `rebar.llm.build_drift.running_build_sha()` already resolves the running
  build's commit, and `BuildDrift` already carries `commits_behind` against a pinned ref.
  That capability is deliberately NOT tracked here.

  Marked `[non-codebase]` because the done-evidence is a decision recorded on Gerrit changes
  2608 and 3014, not an artifact in this repository's tree.
- [x] AC5 [non-codebase] — SETTLED BY REMOVAL, not by repair. The pruner's
  `Directory not empty` failures and the partial release stub `5fb693345b0cd...1559` no
  longer have a subject on this host: `~/.local/state/rebar-dev/` is gone in its entirety,
  along with `~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh`, its `.pre-ac97.bak` backup, all three
  `com.navapbc.rebar-*` LaunchAgents, and `docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md`.

  Measured 2026-09-20 with the sandbox lifted, so these are genuine `ENOENT` results, with
  a control probe confirming `~/.local`, `~/.local/state`, `~/.local/bin` and
  `~/.local/share` all resolve as existing. The full evidence is in the closing comment.

  AC5's two original checks both pass, but VACUOUSLY: the stub is absent because the whole
  `releases` tree is absent, and `Directory not empty` cannot appear in a
  `launchd.err.log` that does not exist. Ticking that as a repair would assert something
  untrue, so it is recorded here as what it is.

  Restore was attempted first, per operator decision, and is not available:
  `~/Desktop/backup` carries neither `.local/` nor `Library/`, and no other copy of the
  updater exists anywhere under `$HOME`. Rebuilding it would be authoring a NEW
  machine-local tool rather than restoring one, which AGENTS.md places outside this
  repository.

  Marked `[non-codebase]` because the done-evidence is the measured state of one operator's
  machine, not an artifact in this repository's tree.

## Testing

Repository-side (AC4), from a worktree with `.venv/bin` first on `PATH`:

```
python -m pytest tests/unit/test_doctor_build_freshness.py -q
python -m pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py -q
make lint
make typecheck
```

`test_doctor_build_freshness.py` is the named coverage for BOTH AC4 signals, not only
`build-stale`: it asserts the `reject-streak` finding at, above and below its threshold and
on a corrupt counter; the `build-stale` finding above and below its threshold and on a sha
absent from the repo; the absent-state `unavailable` path; and that both reach an operator
through `rebar doctor` in text and JSON without altering its exit code.

Host-side (AC1, AC2, AC5) cannot be covered by a repository test: `rebar-dev-update.sh` is
machine-local and git-ignored, so it lies outside any test's reach. Those are proven by the
observations named in their acceptance criteria, run against the live updater, and the
AC2 resolver is exercised against a harness carrying the real pin.

## Constraints

- Do not pin a local update tool. The required uv version moves as `main` moves, so it must
  be read per candidate commit rather than baked into this host.
- The pin cannot be widened: `check_uv_pin.py` fails the build when `required-version` is
  loosened to a range or overridden per call site, because an exact pin is the property
  under test.
